extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, judges, litigators, and IP practitioners working on Brazilian patent prosecution and litigation
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing appeals, motions, licensing (voluntary, offer, compulsory), pharmaceutical-patent specifics, and case-management challenges under Brazilian patent law and the Civil Procedure Code (CPC) and the Industrial Property Law (LPI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The term for appeals is, as a rule, 15 days from the date of publication of the decision, counted in business days; motions for clarification have a five-day term (Article 1,003 of the CPC; Article 219).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are counted in business days; failure to file within the term precludes the party's right to object the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions for clarification (embargos de declaração)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions for clarification aim to clarify obscurity, eliminate contradiction, supply omission, or correct material error in any court decision (Articles 1,022–1,027 of the CPC). They are not primarily intended to modify decisions but may change the court's understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be filed within five days in a petition indicating the error/obscurity/contradiction/omission; no appeal bond required; judge notifies respondent to comment within five days if acceptance would change the decision; judge must decide within five days. Motions have no effect of supersedeas and interrupt the appeal term. Frivolous motions may attract fines up to 2% (increased to 10% for repetition) of the adjusted amount in dispute and can condition future appeals on deposit of the fine (Article 1,026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated appeals under Article 994
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 994 provides the list of appeals allowed under Brazilian law: appeal from final judgment, interlocutory appeal, internal interlocutory appeal, motion for clarification, ordinary appeal, appeal to the STJ, appeal to the STF, interlocutory appeal from an appeal to the STJ or to the STF, and appeal against a divergent decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals generally do not prevent the effectiveness of the decision unless otherwise provided by law or court decision (Article 995).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals may be filed by the losing party, by an aggrieved third party, or by the Public Prosecutor’s Office as a party or legal guardian (Article 996 of the CPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A third party must demonstrate that the decision may affect the right they claim or discuss in court as a procedural substitute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-appeal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If both plaintiff and defendant are defeated, an appeal filed by either may be joined by the other as a cross-appeal in appeals from final judgment or appeals to higher courts (Article 997(1)–(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-appeals are subordinated to the independent appeal and follow the same admissibility and trial rules; a cross-appeal will not be heard if the main appeal is withdrawn or considered inadmissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant may, at any time, without the respondent's consent, withdraw the appeal (Article 998 of the CPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: withdrawal is not permitted for matters in which general repercussion has been recognized and that are subject of repeated appeals to the STF or STJ (Article 998(1)). Parties can also settle and request judicial ratification before or after trial, overruling prior decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal bond/payment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When required by law, the appellant must evidence payment of the appeal bond, including remittance and return fees, under penalty of dismissal (Article 1,007 of the CPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions apply to appeals by the Public Prosecutor’s Office, government entities and those legally exempt. Insufficient payment leads to dismissal if not cured within five days after attorney notification. Remittance and return fees are not required in electronic proceedings (Article 1,007(1)–(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from final judgment — petition content
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal from final judgment must be filed by a petition addressed to the trial court containing: (I) names and identification of the parties; (II) description of the fact and of the right; (III) reasons for the request for change or declaration of nullity; and (IV) the request for a new decision (Articles 1,009–1,014; Article 1,010).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appellee is notified to file a brief within 15 days; if the appellee files a cross-appeal, the judge notifies the appellant to file the brief; the case is forwarded to the appellate court without judgment of admissibility (Article 1,010(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of appeals / supersedeas (efeito suspensivo)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, appeals from final judgment have the effect of supersedeas (suspensive effect) (Article 1,012). However, certain decisions produce immediate effect despite appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions effective immediately include, inter alia: approval of land division, payment of support, dismissal without prejudice in certain cases, arbitration requests granted, confirmation/granting/revocation of provisional injunction, decreeing interdiction, and other hypotheses provided by law (Article 1,012(1)). For cases producing immediate effect, the interested party may request provisional enforcement. A party may request the grant of suspensive effect by demonstrating likelihood of success or risk of serious or irreparable harm; requests may be made to the court between filing and assignment or to the rapporteur once assigned (Article 1,012(2)–(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellate court review powers and possible outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellate court may fully review matters of fact and law submitted to it and may determine measures to the lower court if necessary (Article 1,008; Article 1,013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing an appeal, the court may change a decision that dismissed the case without prejudice; decree decision nullity for lack of congruence; verify omission and judge omitted requests; or decree nullity due to lack of grounds. Matters of fact not presented below may be raised on appeal if due to force majeure (Article 1,014).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory appeal scope (Article 1,015 list)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interlocutory appeal objects to interlocutory decisions and, per Article 1,015, can be filed against items including provisional injunctions; case merits; rejection of arbitration clause; piercing the corporate veil; rejection or revocation of free legal aid; exhibition or possession of document/thing; exclusion of a joint party; limitation of the joinder of parties; admission/non-admission of third-party intervention; granting/modification/revocation of effect of supersedeas to motions to stay execution; reassignment of the burden of proof; and other cases expressly referred to in law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlocutory appeals may also be filed against interlocutory decisions rendered during decision settlement, enforcement, execution, or inventory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory appeal procedure and rapporteur powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Interlocutory appeals are addressed directly to the competent court by petition stating names of the parties, description of fact and right, reasons for change or invalidation, the request, and attorneys' names and addresses (Article 1,016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rapporteur may grant suspensive effect to the appeal, grant interlocutory relief (totally or partially), inform the judge of the decision, order personal notification of the appellee to respond within 15 days attaching necessary documentation, and request a trial date within one month from notification (Articles 1,019–1,020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal interlocutory appeal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An internal interlocutory appeal may be filed against a decision rendered by the rapporteur and is addressed to the rapporteur (Article 1,021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rapporteur notifies the respondent to manifest within 15 days; if no retraction occurs, the rapporteur submits the appeal to judgment by the panel and includes it in the agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to the STF and STJ — scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals to the Federal Supreme Court (STF) and to the Superior Court of Justice (STJ) are available after appellate decisions but their subject-matter is restricted: STF reviews alleged constitutional violations (and requires demonstration of general repercussion), STJ deals with violations of federal law (Articles 1,029–1,034).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STJ/STF may disregard correctable formal defects. As a rule, their decisions do not have suspensive effect; for suspensive effect to be granted one must apply to the higher court or, if assigned, to the rapporteur or court leadership before admissibility is examined. Once admitted, appeals to those courts are limited to matters of law and do not allow review of facts or evidence (Article 1,034).

rubrics_metrics.name: General repercussion requirement for STF appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: For an appeal to the STF, the appellant must demonstrate general repercussion — existence of relevant economic, political, social or legal issues beyond the parties' interests (Article 1,035).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The general repercussion must be demonstrated in a specific chapter of the appeal. If recognized, the rapporteur orders the stay of all pending individual or class proceedings in Brazil on the same issue and the appeal must be heard within one year (Article 1,035(9)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals against divergent decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal may be lodged against a judgment of a fractional court that diverges from another body of the same court on the merits; divergence may be in the application of substantive or procedural law (Articles 1,043–1,044).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal against a divergent decision must follow the procedure established in the internal rules of the respective higher court. A divergence that authorizes such an appeal can occur when the leading appellate decision belongs to the same panel but its composition has been altered by more than half of its members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal prosecution under the LPI
rubrics_metrics.description: The Industrial Property Law (LPI) criminalizes certain conducts; criminal prosecution for LPI crimes generally requires a complaint by the interested party, except for crimes specified as public (Article 199; Article 191 for a public prosecution). Criminal proceedings are regulated by the Code of Criminal Procedure and are processed in criminal courts separate from civil claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal prosecution does not depend on civil lawsuits. Allegation of patent nullity may be used as a defense in criminal prosecution, but acquittal in criminal court does not imply patent nullity, which requires a separate competent action (Article 205).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary license requirements and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Articles 61–63 of the LPI, the patent holder or applicant may enter into a license contract for exploitation. The license contract must be registered with the INPI to produce effects in relation to third parties from the date of its publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is not required for validating evidence of use. The licensee may be vested by the holder with powers to act in defense of the patent. Improvements introduced in a licensed patent belong to the one who makes them, but the other contracting party has a right of first refusal for licensing (Article 63).

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer of license (public offer) procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent holder may request the INPI to place the patent on offer for exploitation; INPI will arrange publication of the offer (Articles 64–67). The holder may withdraw the offer before express acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A voluntary exclusive license cannot be registered or offered without the holder having withdrawn the offer. If parties fail to reach agreement, they may request INPI to arbitrate remuneration, which may be reviewed after one year. The holder may request cancellation of the license if the licensee does not begin effective exploitation within one year, interrupts exploitation for more than one year, or fails to meet exploitation conditions (Article 67).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and nature of compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory licenses are provided in Articles 68–74 of the LPI and may be imposed when the patent holder exercises rights abusively or abuses economic power as evidenced by law or administrative/court decision. Compulsory licenses are always non-exclusive and sublicenses are not permitted (Article 68; Article 72).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various specific grounds and procedures apply depending on the basis for the compulsory license (lack of exploitation, dependence, public interest/emergency, abuse of economic power).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license for lack of exploitation or insufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory license may be granted when the patent's subject matter is not exploited in Brazil due to lack of manufacturing or incomplete manufacturing, lack of full use of a patented process (except in cases of economic impracticability allowing import), or when commercialization does not meet market needs (Article 68, Paragraph 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request can only be made by a person with legitimate interest and with the technical and economic capacity to efficiently exploit the patent, predominantly for the domestic market (Article 68(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-dependent compulsory license conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent-dependent compulsory license is granted when: (I) dependence of one patent on another is characterized; (II) the dependent patent constitutes substantial technical progress over the previous patent; and (III) the holders do not reach an agreement for exploitation (Article 70).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dependent patent is one whose exploitation obligatorily depends on the use of the subject matter of a previous patent; cross-compulsory licenses may be granted to the holder of the dependent patent (Article 70(1)–(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license for national emergency or public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases of national emergency or public interest declared by the federal executive, a temporary nonexclusive compulsory license may be granted if the patent holder or licensee does not meet the need; the judge may grant it at his own initiative and the instrument establishes its term and possible extension (Article 71).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This type of license is temporary and nonexclusive and must respect the rights of the holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to granting compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory license will not be granted if, on the application date, the holder: (I) justifies non-use for legitimate reasons; (II) proves that serious and effective preparations for exploitation have been carried out; or (III) justifies lack of manufacturing or commercialization due to a legal obstacle (Article 69).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These defenses must be supported by evidence and are considered in the administrative or INPI process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative procedure for compulsory license requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for compulsory license must indicate the conditions offered to the patent holder; the holder is notified to present an opinion within 60 days, after which absence of opinion is deemed acceptance under offered conditions (Article 73).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants invoking abuse must attach evidentiary documentation. If requested for lack of exploitation, the patent holder must evidence exploitation. INPI may appoint a commission (including external specialists) to decide compensation; public bodies must provide requested information; INPI decides within 60 days (Article 73(4)–(7)). An appeal against a decision granting a compulsory license does not have suspensive effect (Article 73(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations and limits on compulsory-licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for legitimate reasons, the licensee must begin exploiting the patent within one year of grant (interruptions of one year allowed); failure permits the patent holder to request revocation (Article 74). Licensee is vested with powers to act in defense of the patent; assignment of the compulsory license only allowed when performed jointly with assignment/disposal/leasing of the part that explores it (Article 74(2)–(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where compulsory license is granted for abuse of economic power and the licensee proposes local manufacturing, a limited one-year term to import may be granted provided the product has been placed on the market by the holder or with their consent; import by third parties of products manufactured in accordance with a licensed process/product patent is admitted in these circumstances (Article 68(3)–(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmaceutical patents — pipeline and ANVISA prior consent history
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed before Brazil's ratification of TRIPS were subject to pipeline rules (Law No. 10,196/01 and related provisions) that rejected certain earlier-filed pharma applications. Article 229-C historically required prior consent of ANVISA for granting pharmaceutical patents, a requirement that generated disputes about jurisdiction and scope of ANVISA's review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANVISA was understood to be able to assess public-health harm but not patentability (novelty, inventive step, utility). Law No. 14,195 (2021) repealed the prior-consent requirement, returning sole patent examination/granting competence to INPI and expecting reduction in backlog and analysis time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second medical use and Swiss-type claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the LPI is silent on 'use' claims, INPI accepts second medical use claims provided they are for a new and nonobvious therapeutic application and the mechanism is different from the first use. Protection of second medical use is often effected by linking the use to a manufacturing process (the 'Swiss formula').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: INPI's examination guidelines allow claims for first medical use (a product used as a drug for the first time) and second medical use (a known drug used for a new therapeutic application). Patentable subject matter also includes new/improved methods of extraction, purification, synthesis, chemically modified natural compounds, compositions, transgenic microorganisms, and modified biological processes when nonobvious. Products isolated from nature can be patentable when given practical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key case-management challenges and judicial cooperation (CPC Articles 67–69)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identified practical challenges: lack of court specialization in patent matters; difficulty producing expert evidence; uncertain relation between patent nullity actions and infringement actions. CPC Articles 67–69 establish a duty of reciprocal cooperation among judicial bodies and provide mechanisms for inter-court cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for judicial cooperation must be promptly met and can be executed via direct assistance, joining/attachment of cases, provision of information, or acts between judges. Cooperative acts may include service of process, obtaining and presenting evidence, provisional injunctions, measures for recovery/preservation of companies, centralization of repeated cases, and execution of court decisions. Resolution No. 350/2020 of the National Justice Council regulates national judicial cooperation procedures.
